sampling_model.design: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections at a common baseline and dates \(1,\ldots,T\), with cohort \(g\) treated from date \(g\) onward.
sampling_model.units: Independent Gaussian cohort-time cell means with known variance \(\sigma^2/(Nq_g)\) at each wave.
sampling_model.treatment: For each \(t\le T-m\), cohort \(g\le t\) is compared with pooled set \(C_t\); no untreated cohort remains for the target at \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed shares satisfy \(c_q/T\le q_g\le C_q/T\), and \(q_{>t}>0\) at every score date.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated inside the exact known-covariance score experiment. The Holder calendar path and bounded centered cohort deviations define one convex parameter class, and the estimator is computed from a finite-dimensional covariance-weighted modulus optimization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 3.3, Proposition 5, shows that sufficiently long-run nonnegative weighted effects are not identified without extrapolation when no never-treated units remain.
The paper identifies group-time ATTs, defines calendar aggregations, and provides simultaneous inference for identified collections.
Proposition 1 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function and its efficiency bound for the two-period ATT.
Gaussian linear-functional difficulty is characterized through a modulus, and affine minimax rules are near global minimax rules.
Known-variance Gaussian confidence procedures over convex regression classes are characterized by ordered moduli and sharp expected-length bounds.
Theorem 3.1 on pp. 15--16 derives a simple honest interval and its Holder boundary bias--variance calibration for nonparametric regression.
Uniformly valid DiD confidence sets are constructed under bounded post-treatment deviations from observed pre-trends.
Loewner covariance dominance and Anderson's theorem order Gaussian procedures for symmetric convex acceptance regions.

body.tldr: A fixed-cohort repeated-cross-section event study induces an exact Gaussian score experiment with shrinking not-yet-treated pools and nested shared-baseline dependence. For the causal terminal calendar ATT, the finite-dimensional covariance-weighted modulus \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) now gives the operator-specific frontier: global minimax MSE is bounded above and below by explicit universal multiples of its square, and shortest uniformly honest expected length is bounded by explicit \(\alpha\)-dependent multiples of the modulus. Total measurable affine estimators and bias-aware intervals attain the upper bounds, with exact finite-sample coverage. The matched-date-block calculation remains a separate \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\) calibration. Converting the nested modulus to the candidate closed-form calendar functional is open because the proposed dimension-free bounded lift is impossible.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD work explains why valid long-run comparisons disappear, while Gaussian optimal-recovery theory begins with a supplied observation operator and covariance. Neither literature derives the exact nested shared-baseline score geometry and states the resulting global MSE and honest-length frontier for a terminal causal calendar ATT.
project_justification.niche: The contribution is the exact operator-specific inference problem generated by fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections: a computable finite-dimensional nested covariance modulus, rather than an unsupported scalar phase approximation.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the Gaussian score covariance, proves explicit two-point lower bounds and affine upper bounds for global minimax MSE and honest expected length, supplies a total bias-aware interval with exact coverage, and isolates conversion of the exact modulus to a closed-form calendar rate as the remaining mathematical question.

body.related_work: Callaway and Sant'Anna supply the group-time causal effects and calendar aggregation underlying the target. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess show in Section 3.3, Proposition 5, why sufficiently long-run effects lose valid comparisons, motivating extrapolation but not providing its inference frontier. Donoho's 1994 Gaussian model in equation (1), Theorem 1, and Section 11 supplies general modulus and affine-minimax architecture conditional on known operators and weights. Armstrong and Kolesar's 2018 Section 3.2, equations (23)--(26), develops bias-aware Gaussian intervals for supplied regression operators, and their 2020 equation (15) and Theorem 3.1 on pages 15--16 give a direct-regression Holder calibration. None of those results derives a bounded right inverse for the shared-baseline Gram term. The present contribution therefore stops at the exact nested modulus frontier. The matched-date-block proposition concerns only \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\) and does not order or approximate the nested experiment.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A dimension-free lift matching Holder localization, bounded-deviation leverage, and shared-baseline Mahalanobis energy cannot satisfy the claimed \(T/k^2\) energy bound already for equal shares, \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). Consequently the exact nested modulus has no proved closed-form calendar rate or phase diagram here. The matched comparison deletes only cross-date dependence after preserving each full within-date covariance block; it is a \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\) sanity experiment and cannot be transferred to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\). The Gaussian model also leaves non-Gaussian coupling, nuisance estimation, and smoothness adaptation outside the present guarantee.
body.honest_scope: Established results are the exact score covariance, total measurable modulus procedures, explicit global MSE and honest-length comparisons with \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\), exact finite-sample interval coverage, and the separate matched-date-block calculation. No bounded right inverse, equivalence with \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), nested homogeneous rate, or closed-form nested phase diagram is claimed. Whether the exact nested modulus admits another useful calendar-scale characterization remains open; the adaptation question must respect that unresolved conversion.
body.interpretation: The exact modulus is actionable: for the observed calendar and cohort shares, solve its finite-dimensional convex optimization, use the exposed direction in the stated affine estimator, and report the corresponding bias-aware interval. Its value measures all smoothness, cohort-heterogeneity, and shared-baseline effects jointly. The candidate scalar functional \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) may be useful diagnostically, but no proved uniform equivalence licenses it as the nested-experiment rate.
